claims.statement: Existing benchmarks (CoreMark, MLMark, MLPerf inference) do not adequately address the unique constraints of TinyML systems: they lack energy measurement, require too much memory, or are not designed for MCU-class hardware.
confidence_reasons: Authors' qualitative argument; no controlled comparison experiment
CoreMark omission of ML and power is factual; MLMark memory requirement is stated as a fact

claims.statement: MLPerf Tiny measures three axes — accuracy, latency (inferences per second), and energy (µJ/inference) — for each of its four benchmarks.
confidence_reasons: Measurement protocol defined in detail in §5.3 and Appendix A

claims.statement: MLPerf Tiny v0.5 comprises four benchmarks: keyword spotting (DS-CNN, Speech Commands v2, 90% accuracy target), visual wake words (MobileNetV1, MSCOCO 2014, 80% accuracy target), image classification (ResNetv1, CIFAR-10, 85% accuracy target), and anomaly detection (FC autoencoder, DCASE2020 Toy-car, 0.85 AUC target).
confidence_reasons: Fully specified in paper Table 1 and §4

claims.statement: The DS-CNN KWS reference model achieves 92.2% accuracy in the authors' experiments; the quantized version achieves 91.6% on the full test set and 91.7% on a 1,000-utterance subset.
The AD reference model (fp32) achieves AUC 0.88; the quantized version achieves AUC 0.86 on the 248-sample evaluation set.

The first MLPerf Tiny submission round (v0.5, June 2021) received five diverse submissions spanning ARM MCU, RISC-V MCU, neural network accelerator, software-only toolchain (Raspberry Pi 4), and FPGA platforms.
INT-8 post-training quantization is the most common numerical format across v0.5 submissions.
confidence_reasons: Table 2 lists 4 of 5 submissions using INT-8 PTQ; observation is directly supported

claims.statement: The modular closed/open division design enabled submitters with different goals — hardware performance, software optimization, precision quantization — to participate in the same benchmark round.
confidence_reasons: Evidence shows diverse submission types; interpretation that this is due to the modular design is stated by authors but not experimentally isolated

claims.statement: No v0.5 submission modified the training dataset, suggesting TinyML design at this stage is primarily focused on models, frameworks, and hardware rather than data.
confidence_reasons: Directly observed from Table 2; causal interpretation ('suggesting') is appropriately hedged

claims.statement: The power consumption of v0.5 platforms ranged from µWatts to Watts.
confidence_reasons: Stated in paper §6.2; exact per-platform values not given

limitations.statement: The gap characterization of prior benchmarks is qualitative; no controlled performance comparison was run.
Reference model accuracy values are single-run results with no variance reported; seed-to-seed or run-to-run stability is unknown.
The v0.5 round is the first submission round only; patterns observed (e.g. INT-8 dominance, no dataset modifications) may change in future rounds.
Pre-processing and streaming input are excluded from the measurement window, which may not reflect real-world TinyML deployment performance.
Closed division models are limited to FC and CNN architectures; RNN and other architectures are not in the reference implementations.
